title: Literary style
summary: Read Turkish narrative prose: how a story moves between `-DI`, `-mIş` and the historical present, how long sentences are built from `-(y)Ip` and `-(y)ArAk`, what older forms such as *gidesim geldi* and *-cAsInA* add, how writers move words after the verb for rhythm, and how free indirect speech lets the narrator speak in a character's voice.
canDo: Follow the tense switches of a story and say what each one does
Recognize literary forms such as gidesim geldi, doyasıya and -cAsInA, and use the first
Say why a writer has moved a word after the verb, and read an older couplet in prose order
Recognize free indirect speech and rewrite a thought in it
